note: George M. Pullman married Harriett Sanger on 13 June 1867; their children were Florence (1868-1937), Harriett (1869-1956) and the twins George, Jr. (1875-1901) and Walter Sanger, known as Sanger (1875-1905). The twins' 'activities and affairs filled many column inches'; as boys they were schooled at home on Prairie Avenue, allegedly 'arranging and promoting pit bull fights'; as teenagers 'frequently were seen riding around Chicago in cabs filled with champagne bottles'; at Harvard Training School they ranked 147 and 148 out of 148. Pullman's will gave them $3,000 a year. George, Jr. secretly married Lynn Fernald, 'his brother's betrothed'; Sanger moved in with an unnamed woman, a common-law marriage dissolved when his mother 'paid the unnamed woman $10,000 to leave Sanger and never return'. Both sought the Keeley Cure. Sanger, 'widely acknowledged as the smarter of the 2, was very poor with money', was expelled from the New York Athletic Club for non-payment of dues, and in 1901 his sister-in-law's luggage was held five months by a creditor. Frederick Bowers sued George for $100,000, 'eventually settling for $50,000'. George died of pneumonia complications in November 1901; Sanger 'died after being thrown from a horse and carriage after yet another wild ride in August, 1905'. The World, 1901: 'Death of George Pullman a Warning to Rich Fathers.'
